about.title: Culver City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Culver City families are often left sorting through grief while also facing unfamiliar legal deadlines. Los Angeles County recorded 80 injury collisions and 113 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with one traffic death — a reminder that even a single loss ripples through an entire household. Corridors such as Washington Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and the I-405 see steady traffic volume, and collisions there can escalate quickly. California law gives close family members, and in some cases dependents, a path to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that path has real time limits and specific rules about who may file. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent, contingency-based attorney who can walk through what happened, what the law allows, and what steps might come next.

whyChoose.title: What Culver City Families Should Know

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing primarily to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with certain other dependents or heirs eligible in specific situations. An independent attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Two-Year Window Is Firm
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity — such as a public roadway agency — can require action much sooner. Missing these deadlines can close off options permanently, so timing matters.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Financial Support
items.desc: California law recognizes that a wrongful death claim can include lost financial support and funeral costs, but also the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided. This is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges connected to the same crash.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those family members exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Does a criminal case against the driver affect our civil claim?
items.answer: No — a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver may face. The two proceed on different timelines and under different rules, and a criminal outcome isn't required for a civil claim to move forward. Your family can pursue a civil claim regardless of what happens in criminal court.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash near a Culver City intersection with heavy traffic, like along Washington Boulevard. Does that location matter for our claim?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't determine fault, but public collision records for corridors like Washington Boulevard can be part of the evidence an attorney reviews. What matters most is how the crash happened and who was involved. An independent attorney can look at the specific facts of your case rather than assumptions about any particular road.
